title: The winter California turned into a lake 🌊
subject: flood
description:
Could a storm like 1862 hit California again? 👇

In the winter of 1861–62, about 43 days of storms filled the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys into an inland sea about 300 miles long. Governor Leland Stanford rowed to his inauguration, at least 4,000 people died, and the USGS ARkStorm scenario estimates a repeat today would cost about $725 billion.

Sources: USGS ("ARkStorm Scenario", "ARkStorm: California's Other 'Big One'"), William H. Brewer, "Up and Down California in 1860–1864", Wikipedia ("Great Flood of 1862")

scenes.text: California once had a lake 300 miles long.
In the winter of 1861, about 43 days of storms filled the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys into one inland sea.
On January 10, 1862, Leland Stanford rowed a boat to his inauguration as governor.
Botanist William Brewer wrote, "Thousands of farms are entirely under water." At least 4,000 people died.
The legislature fled to San Francisco.
The USGS modeled a repeat: $725 billion in losses and 1.5 million people evacuated.
